extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, and practitioners preparing ex parte appeals to the USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for filing and prosecuting ex parte appeals before the USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board, including who may appeal, when and how to file a notice of appeal, appeal/reply brief rules, deadlines, fees, hearings, decisions, rehearing, and related resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can file a notice of appeal — patent applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for a patent, any of whose claims has been twice rejected, may appeal from the decision of the primary examiner to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, having once paid the fee for such appeal. (35 U.S.C. 134(a); 37 C.F.R. 41.31(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every applicant, any of whose claims has been twice rejected, may appeal by filing a notice of appeal accompanied by the fee set forth in §41.20(b)(1) within the time period provided under §1.134 for reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can file a notice of appeal — patent owner (reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner in a reexamination may appeal from the final rejection of any claim by the primary examiner to the Board, having once paid the fee for such appeal. (35 U.S.C. 134(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. 41.31(a)(2) covers ex parte reexaminations filed before November 29, 1999 (any claim twice rejected). 37 C.F.R. 41.31(a)(3) covers ex parte reexaminations filed on or after November 29, 1999 (any claim finally rejected). Fee payment and timing requirements per the cited rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to file a notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing differs by status: an applicant may file upon any claim being twice rejected; a patent owner in reexamination files upon final rejection (or twice rejected depending on filing date relative to Nov 29, 1999).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: 35 U.S.C. 134(a) and 134(b); 37 C.F.R. 41.31(a)(1)-(a)(3). The page emphasizes the different triggers (twice rejected vs. finally rejected) depending on applicant vs. reexamination and the reexamination filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file a Notice of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: File Notice of Appeal using form AIA/31 and pay required fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also note the appeal is 'presumed to be taken from the rejection of all claims under rejection unless canceled by an amendment filed by the applicant and entered by the Office' (37 C.F.R. 41.31(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal claims presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal, when taken, is presumed to be taken from the rejection of all claims under rejection unless canceled by an amendment filed by the applicant and entered by the Office. (37 C.F.R. 41.31(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant wishes to narrow which claims are on appeal, ensure any amendments to cancel claims are filed and entered by the Office; otherwise the appeal covers all rejected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief — filing to preserve appellant's rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal brief must be filed to preserve appellant’s right to the appealed claims notwithstanding circumstances such as: (A) petition to invoke Director supervisory authority under 37 CFR 1.181; (B) filing of an amendment (even one the examiner indicated may place claims in condition for allowance) unless the examiner, in acting on the amendment, disposes of all issues on appeal; (C) receipt of a letter from the examiner stating prosecution is suspended, without the examiner withdrawing the final rejection from which appeal has been taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an appeal brief preserves the appeal even when other procedural steps (petitions, amendments) are taken unless the examiner explicitly resolves all appealed issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief — deadlines and extension rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Must file the appeal brief within 2 months from the date of filing the Notice of Appeal; no extension of time is required or permitted for that 2‑month period even if it falls after a shortened statutory period. (37 C.F.R. 41.37(a); MPEP 1205.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing after the initial 2‑month period and prior to a 3‑month shortened statutory period for reply set in the Office Action, a petition for a one month extension of time is required. Extensions of time are governed by 37 C.F.R. 41.37 and MPEP 1205.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief — fee and assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal brief must be accompanied by the payment of any appeal brief fee set forth in 37 C.F.R. 41.20(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board provides an appeal brief template and instructions (see 'Preparing an Ex Parte Appeal Brief' webpage) to help appellants prepare compliant briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of not filing an appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant does not file an appeal brief the appeal will be dismissed and the application usually goes abandoned if the application contains no allowed claims. If there are allowed claims, the application is not abandoned and the appellant may petition to reinstate the claims and the appeal but must meet strict requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reinstate an appeal when allowed claims exist, appellant must file a petition (with petition fee) showing facts equivalent to a petition to revive under 37 C.F.R. 1.137, and either (1) file an RCE accompanied by a submission (reply under 37 C.F.R. 1.111) and fees, or (2) file an appeal brief and appeal brief fee to reinstate the appeal. If claims are objected to as dependent on a rejected claim and no allowed claims exist, the appeal will be dismissed and the application abandoned. See MPEP 1205.01 and MPEP § 711.03(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Answer — new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s answer may contain a new ground of rejection, either designated or undesignated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references procedures for responding to new grounds of rejection in an examiner’s answer (see MPEP § 1207.03 and related guidance). If a new ground is present, special response options and timing apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief — timing, extensions, and governing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A single reply brief may be filed as a matter of right within the later of two months from the date of either the examiner’s answer or a decision refusing to grant a petition under 37 C.F.R. 1.181. (37 C.F.R. 41.41(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time to file the reply brief may be granted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. 1.136(b) (for patent applications) or 1.550(c) (for ex parte reexamination proceedings). Extensions under 37 C.F.R. 1.136(a) are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief — when filing is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally a reply brief is not required; if appellant does not file a reply brief within the two month period, the application will be forwarded to the Board for decision. However, a reply brief (or a reply under 37 C.F.R. 1.111 to reopen prosecution) is required in response to: (A) an examiner’s answer that designates a new ground of rejection (37 C.F.R. 41.39); or (B) a substitute examiner’s answer after a Board remand for further consideration where the substitute may contain a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When required, failure to file the required reply may affect the ability to maintain the appeal or require reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal forwarding fee and other fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain fees are required at stages of the appeal process, including the Notice of Appeal fee, appeal brief fee (37 C.F.R. 41.20(b)(2)), and an appeal forwarding fee where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee and payment information is provided on USPTO pages. Additional fees referenced include RCE fees (37 C.F.R. 1.17(e)) if prosecution is to continue after Board decision and petition fees for reinstatement or other petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting and conducting an oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant may request an oral hearing using form AIA/32 (Request for Oral Hearing Before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to guidance on requesting an oral hearing and conducting hearings before the Board. Appellants should follow the Board’s procedures and any scheduling/formatting requirements in the hearing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision types and immediate consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Board decisions may be Affirmed, Affirmed‑in‑part, or Reversed. Affirmed: jurisdiction over an application or patent under ex parte reexamination passes to the examiner for any further action. Affirmed‑in‑part: the decision reverses all rejections pertaining to at least one, but not all, claims. Reversed: complete reversal of the examiner’s rejection(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If affirmed, proceedings are terminated unless an appeal to a court or civil action is timely filed, except where claims stand allowed or the decision requires further examiner action (37 C.F.R. 41.54; 1.197(a)). To continue prosecution after the Board’s decision, an amendment presenting new or amended claims together with an RCE under 37 C.F.R. 1.114 and fee (1.17(e)) may be filed. On reversal, the case is brought up for immediate examiner action; the examiner should not undertake a new search to find new references but, if the examiner knows of particular references indicating nonpatentability, the examiner should seek authorization (TC Director/CRU) under 37 C.F.R. 1.198 to reopen prosecution to enter a new rejection. See MPEP 1214.04 and MPEP § 706.07(h)(XI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for rehearing — timing and content limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant may file a request for rehearing within two (2) months of the date of the original decision of the Board. The request must 'state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked by the Board.' Arguments not previously raised and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted except as provided in 37 C.F.R. 41.52(a)(2)-(a)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No request for rehearing from a decision on rehearing is permitted unless the rehearing decision so modified the original decision as to become, in effect, a new decision AND the Board states that a second request for rehearing would be permitted. (37 C.F.R. 41.52(a)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tips, checklists, and common reasons for non‑compliant briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board publishes practice tips and checklists to reduce non‑compliant briefs, including a listing of the top eight reasons briefs are found to be non‑compliant and forms used to notify parties of non‑compliant briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants should consult the 'Practice tips for writing effective appeal briefs' and the checklists to avoid the most common compliance errors; templates and instructional materials are available on the USPTO site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing rules and reference materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeals process is governed by Board rules, the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) chapters, and specific Code of Federal Regulations provisions cited throughout (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 134; 37 C.F.R. parts 1, 41).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key references listed include: MPEP Chapter 1200 (appeals), MPEP Chapter 2200 (ex parte reexamination), MPEP Chapter 2600 (inter partes reexamination), and Board rules for appeals filed before January 2012. Use these authorities for detailed procedural and substantive requirements.
